UADataType.Description: The ControlModeEnumeration contains the PackML modes of operation of a machine.

Field.Name: OTHER
Field.Description: This state is used if no other state below applies.

Field.Name: PRODUCTION
Field.Description: Primary Mode used for all production activities, All PackML model states will be utilized. The unit/machine executes relevant logic in response to commands which are mainly coming from External Systems, or entered directly by the operator.

Field.Name: MAINTENANCE
Field.Description: Used for routine preventive Maintenance or planned maintenance. Shall be utilized to document planned maintenance occurrence and duration. This mode allows authorized personnel to run the unit/machine independent of other systems. This mode would typically be used for fault finding, machine trials, or testing operational improvements. For example: The cleaning of a print head is maintenance.

Field.Name: MANUAL
Field.Description: Used for fault diagnosis of unplanned technical intervention.

Field.Name: CHANGE OVER
Field.Description: Used specifically for format or recipe change over, includes “cleaning” operations.

Field.Name: CLEAN
Field.Description: Used for Routine Cleaning requirements example: as specified by factory maintenance procedures.

Field.Name: SET UP
Field.Description: Used for set up or adjustments example: mechanical adjustments and testing.

Field.Name: EMPTY OUT
Field.Description: Used to empty out machine example: end of a block of shifts prior to factory weekend shut down, empty out resident product within the machine that could be sent to finished product and minimize part finished “rework”.

Field.Name: REMOTE SERVICE
Field.Description: Used when the machine is serviced remotely, which is a form of remote maintenance. Remark. The Remote Service mode fulfil the safety requirements of the harmonized norm EN415-10:2011 (Safety of packaging machines).

uax:Description.uax:Text: This state is used if no other state below applies.

UADataType.Description: The MaterialDefinitionType structure contains the definition of a material. It is harmonised with ISA 95 Material Definition.

Field.Name: ID
Field.Description: Unique identifier for the material definition.

Field.Name: MES_ID
Field.Description: Unique identifier for the material definition in an external system, e.g. MES.

Field.Name: Description
Field.Description: Description of the material definition.

Field.Name: BaseUnitOfMeasure
Field.Description: The base unit of measure for the material definition.

Field.Name: BatchManaged
Field.Description: If BatchManaged is True, the material lots of this material definition require a unique identification, often called BatchID. The material lots are also called batches in some contexts.

Field.Name: GroupID
Field.Description: The material group the material definition belongs to.

Field.Name: ParentGroupID
Field.Description: The parent group of the material group the material definition belongs to.

Field.Name: ShelfLife
Field.Description: The number of days of usable life for the material definition. The usable life is counted from the production date.

Field.Name: Properties
Field.Description: An array containing additional properties that can be additionally required for the material definition.

Field.Description: The material sublot to be used.

Field.Name: FollowUpMaterials

UADataType.Description: The MaterialLotType structure contains the material lot information. It is harmonised with ISA 95 Material Lot.

Field.Name: ID
Field.Description: Unique identifier for the material lot in the underlying system.

Field.Name: MES_ID
Field.Description: The unique identifier for the material lot in higher level systems. In some production contexts the material lot is called a batch.

Field.Name: Description
Field.Description: Description of the material lot.

Field.Name: MaterialDefinition
Field.Description: The material definition of the material lot.

Field.Name: Status
Field.Description: The stock status of the material lot.

Field.Name: ProductionDate
Field.Description: The date and time when the material lot was produced.

Field.Name: BestUsedBeforeDate
Field.Description: The last date the material lot can be used. It is computed adding the material definition shelf life to the production date.

Field.Name: Properties
Field.Description: An array containing additional properties that can be additionally required for the material lot.

UADataType.Description: The MaterialPointType structure provides the description of the capability of a load or unload point.

Field.Name: ID
Field.Description: Unique identifier for the material point type.

Field.Name: Description
Field.Description: Description of the material point type.

Field.Name: MaterialCapability
Field.Description: The complete set of material definitions that the material point can process.

Field.Name: ConnectedMaterialPoint
Field.Description: The identifier for the node id of the connected material point.

Field.Name: PropagatesProductionOrder
Field.Description: The material point propagates the production order with the ConnectedMaterialPoint. If the material point is a MaterialLoadingPointType, and PropagatesProductionOrder is True, then the material point receives a production order from the upstream ConnectedMaterialPoint. If the material point is a MaterialOutputPointType, and PropagatesProductionOrder is True, then the material point sends a production order to the downstream ConnectedMaterialPoint. If the material point is a MaterialRejectionPointType, and PropagatesProductionOrder is True, then the material point sends a production order to the downstream ConnectedMaterialPoint. This variable is defined by the end user and entered by the developer of the TMC server invoking the SetNewSpecification method.

UADataType.Description: The MaterialStorageBufferDataType structure provides the description of the capability of a material storage buffer.

Field.Name: ID
Field.Description: Unique identifier for the material storage buffer.

Field.Name: StoredMaterial
Field.Description: The material definition for material that can be stored in the material storage buffer.

Field.Name: EngineeringUnits
Field.Description: The unit of measure for the material stored in the buffer.

Field.Name: TotalStorageCapacity
Field.Description: The total capacity of the material storage buffer.

Field.Name: StorageLogic
Field.Description: The logic by which product is loaded and unloaded from the material storage buffer.

Field.Name: MixingLogic
Field.Description: How different material loaded into the material storage buffer mix.

UADataType.Description: The MaterialSublotType structure contains the material sublot information. It is harmonised with ISA 95 Material Sublot.

Field.Name: ID
Field.Description: Unique identifier for the material sublot in the underlying system.

Field.Name: MES_ID
Field.Description: The unique identifier for the material sublot in higher level systems.

Field.Name: MaterialLot
Field.Description: The material lot the sublot belongs to.

Field.Name: MaterialStorageLocationID
Field.Description: Unique identifier for the location where the material is produced/stored.

Field.Name: Quantity
Field.Description: The quantity of the sublot in the base unit of measure defined in the MaterialDefinition.

Field.Name: CarrierID
Field.Description: The ID of the carrier holding the sublot, for example the bobbin core fitted with an RFID. If the sublot is not contained in any carrier, then the CarrierID is NULL.

Field.Name: RelativePositionID
Field.Description: The unique identifier of the relative position of the sublot in the carrier identified by CarrierID. If CarrierID is NULL, then the string is empty.

Field.Name: ParentSublotID
Field.Description: The parent sublot ID is the unique identifier of the material sublot that contains the sublot structure in question. If the sublot is not contained in any sublot, then the ParentSublotID is NULL.

Field.Name: Sublots
Field.Description: The material sublots contained in the material sublot in question.

Field.Name: LocalText

UADataType.Description: The MethodExecutionFeedbackType provides suitable feedback, both positive and negative, to an OPC UA client invoking a method.

UADataType.Description: The ProductionOrderHeaderType structure contains the header information for a production order.

Field.Name: Number
Field.Description: The production order number.

Field.Name: ProducedMaterial
Field.Description: The finished good that the material is produced by the production order.

Field.Name: TargetQuantity
Field.Description: The quantity of ProducedMaterial that is requested by the production order.

Field.Name: ContinueAtJobEnd
Field.Description: When ContinueAtJobEnd is True, then the operator may continue production (overproduction) after fulfilling the required TargetQuantity.

Field.Name: TargetStartTime
Field.Description: The planned start date and time.

Field.Name: TargetEndTime
Field.Description: The planned end date and time.

Field.Name: DataSetID
Field.Description: The identifier of the dataset to be used for the production order, when the dataset is late-bound. The DatasetID will be NULL when the dataset is not late-bound.

Field.Name: DataSetDescription
Field.Description: The description of the dataset.

Field.Name: MaterialListID
Field.Description: The identifier of the material list to be used for the production order, when the material list is late-bound. The DatasetID will be NULL when the dataset is not late-bound.

Field.Name: MaterialListDescription
Field.Description: The description of the material list.

UADataType.Description: The ProductionOrderType structure contains the complete production order information.

Field.Name: Header
Field.Description: The header of the production order.

Field.Name: MaterialList
Field.Description: The material list for the production order.

Field.Name: DataSet
Field.Description: The dataset for the production order.

UADataType.Description: The RootCauseGroupType structure contains a root cause message and its group identifier.

Field.Description: The ID of the group containing the root cause group identified by Id. By means of the ParentID, multiple nested groups are allowed.

Field.Description: The human-readable description of the root cause group identified by the unique identifier.

The OperatorControl variable qualifies the source of the ProcessControlItem Value when RemoteControl is False, otherwise OperatorControl is undefined. When OperatorControl is True, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is modified by the operator with respect to the nominal value, e.g. NominalRate, a.k.a. design speed for a speed control loop. When OperatorControl is False, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is not modified by the operator.

The RemoteControl variable lets the underlying system expose which system is currently in control of the ProcessControlItem. More specifically, if RemoteControl is True, the underlying system copies the RemoteValue to the ProcesControlItem Value to drive it, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is remotely controlled. If RemoteControl is False, the underlying system is not using RemoteValue to drive the ProcessControlItem, but another value that is exposed as the ProcessControlItem Value, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is locally controlled. A client requests (resp. releases) control of the ProcessControlItem by setting RemoteControl to True (resp. False) preferably by invoking the SetRemoteControl Method. If the client does not support methods, then the client sets RemoteControl to True. The underlying system will reset RemoteControl to False if remote control is not activated.

The RemoteControlEnable variable exposes when the underlying system is ready to activate the RemoteControl upon a request by a client. When RemoteControlEnable is False, the underlying system is not ready and will not activate a request to remotely control the ProcessControlItem.
The value set by the client to override the object value.

The accumulated total of the valid value for the last AggregationWindow samples and after the last reset. It is only reset by the successful execution of the ResetAggregates method.

The Property RootCauseGroupList is the list of groups that root causes can be grouped in. They are defined by the end user.

The Property RootCauseList is the complete list of the root causes that the end user has defined to classify and organize the downtime due to the machine module stops. The RootCauseList is user defined.

The Property RootCauseListInputIsMandatory is true when the operator is mandatorily required to select the root cause that best describes the current stop situation. For micro- stops such requirement does not apply.

UAObjectType.Description: The ProcessControlItem Object Type describes a generic control loop including the measured variable to be controlled (PV), the desired value for the variable (SP) and the signal to the actuator (CV) to bring the PV to match the SP.

UAVariable.Description: The OperatorControl variable qualifies the source of the ProcessControlItem Value when RemoteControl is False, otherwise OperatorControl is undefined. When OperatorControl is True, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is modified by the operator with respect to the nominal value, e.g. NominalRate, a.k.a. design speed for a speed control loop. When OperatorControl is False, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is not modified by the operator.

The RemoteControl variable lets the underlying system expose which system is currently in control of the ProcessControlItem. More specifically, if RemoteControl is True, the underlying system copies the RemoteValue to the ProcesControlItem Value to drive it, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is remotely controlled. If RemoteControl is False, the underlying system is not using RemoteValue to drive the ProcessControlItem, but another value that is exposed as the ProcessControlItem Value, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is locally controlled. A client requests (resp. releases) control of the ProcessControlItem by setting RemoteControl to True (resp. False) preferably by invoking the SetRemoteControl Method. If the client does not support methods, then the client sets RemoteControl to True. The underlying system will reset RemoteControl to False if remote control is not activated.

The RemoteControlEnable variable exposes when the underlying system is ready to activate the RemoteControl upon a request by a client. When RemoteControlEnable is False, the underlying system is not ready and will not activate a request to remotely control the ProcessControlItem.
The value set by the client to override the object value.

The OperatorControl variable qualifies the source of the ProcessControlItem Value when RemoteControl is False, otherwise OperatorControl is undefined. When OperatorControl is True, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is modified by the operator with respect to the nominal value, e.g. NominalRate, a.k.a. design speed for a speed control loop. When OperatorControl is False, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is not modified by the operator.

The RemoteControl variable lets the underlying system expose which system is currently in control of the ProcessControlItem. More specifically, if RemoteControl is True, the underlying system copies the RemoteValue to the ProcesControlItem Value to drive it, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is remotely controlled. If RemoteControl is False, the underlying system is not using RemoteValue to drive the ProcessControlItem, but another value that is exposed as the ProcessControlItem Value, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is locally controlled. A client requests (resp. releases) control of the ProcessControlItem by setting RemoteControl to True (resp. False) preferably by invoking the SetRemoteControl Method. The OperatorControl variable qualifies the source of the ProcessControlItem Value when RemoteControl is False, otherwise OperatorControl is undefined. When OperatorControl is True, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is modified by the operator with respect to the nominal value, e.g. NominalRate, a.k.a. design speed for a speed control loop. When OperatorControl is False, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is not modified by the operator.

The RemoteControl variable lets the underlying system expose which system is currently in control of the ProcessControlItem. More specifically, if RemoteControl is True, the underlying system copies the RemoteValue to the ProcesControlItem Value to drive it, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is remotely controlled. If RemoteControl is False, the underlying system is not using RemoteValue to drive the ProcessControlItem, but another value that is exposed as the ProcessControlItem Value, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is locally controlled. A client requests (resp. releases) control of the ProcessControlItem by setting RemoteControl to True (resp. False) preferably by invoking the SetRemoteControl Method. If the client does not support methods, then the client sets RemoteControl to True. The underlying system will reset RemoteControl to False if remote control is not activated.

The RemoteControlEnable variable exposes when the underlying system is ready to activate the RemoteControl upon a request by a client. When RemoteControlEnable is False, the underlying system is not ready and will not activate a request to remotely control the ProcessControlItem.
The value set by the client to override the object value.

The OperatorControl variable qualifies the source of the ProcessControlItem Value when RemoteControl is False, otherwise OperatorControl is undefined. When OperatorControl is True, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is modified by the operator with respect to the nominal value, e.g. NominalRate, a.k.a. design speed for a speed control loop. When OperatorControl is False, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is not modified by the operator.

The RemoteControl variable lets the underlying system expose which system is currently in control of the ProcessControlItem. More specifically, if RemoteControl is True, the underlying system copies the RemoteValue to the ProcesControlItem Value to drive it, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is remotely controlled. If RemoteControl is False, the underlying system is not using RemoteValue to drive the ProcessControlItem, but another value that is exposed as the ProcessControlItem Value, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is locally controlled. A client requests (resp. releases) control of the ProcessControlItem by setting RemoteControl to True (resp. False) preferably by invoking the SetRemoteControl Method. If the client does not support methods, then the client sets RemoteControl to True. The underlying system will reset RemoteControl to False if remote control is not activated.

The RemoteControlEnable variable exposes when the underlying system is ready to activate the RemoteControl upon a request by a client. When RemoteControlEnable is False, the underlying system is not ready and will not activate a request to remotely control the ProcessControlItem.
The value set by the client to override the object value.

The OperatorControl variable qualifies the source of the ProcessControlItem Value when RemoteControl is False, otherwise OperatorControl is undefined. When OperatorControl is True, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is modified by the operator with respect to the nominal value, e.g. NominalRate, a.k.a. design speed for a speed control loop. When OperatorControl is False, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is not modified by the operator.

The RemoteControl variable lets the underlying system expose which system is currently in control of the ProcessControlItem. More specifically, if RemoteControl is True, the underlying system copies the RemoteValue to the ProcesControlItem Value to drive it, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is remotely controlled. If RemoteControl is False, the underlying system is not using RemoteValue to drive the ProcessControlItem, but another value that is exposed as the ProcessControlItem Value, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is locally controlled. A client requests (resp. releases) control of the ProcessControlItem by setting RemoteControl to True (resp. False) preferably by invoking the SetRemoteControl Method. If the client does not support methods, then the client sets RemoteControl to True. The underlying system will reset RemoteControl to False if remote control is not activated.

The RemoteControlEnable variable exposes when the underlying system is ready to activate the RemoteControl upon a request by a client. When RemoteControlEnable is False, the underlying system is not ready and will not activate a request to remotely control the ProcessControlItem.
The value set by the client to override the object value.

When WatchdogEnable is True, if a ProcessControlLoop component’s RemoteControl is True and the time between two consecutive writes of the RemoteAnalogMeasurement is longer than WatchdogTimeout, then the underlying system will generate an alarm, set RemoteControl to False and take control of the loop. When WatchdogEnable is False, no watchdog alarm is generated.
The longest time between two write actions before a watchdog alarm is generated by the underlying system. The value is expressed in milliseconds.

The Property RootCauseList is the complete list of the root causes that the end user has defined to classify and organize the downtime due to the machine module stops. The RootCauseList is user defined.

The OperatorControl variable qualifies the source of the ProcessControlItem Value when RemoteControl is False, otherwise OperatorControl is undefined. When OperatorControl is True, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is modified by the operator with respect to the nominal value, e.g. NominalRate, a.k.a. design speed for a speed control loop. When OperatorControl is False, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is not modified by the operator.

The RemoteControl variable lets the underlying system expose which system is currently in control of the ProcessControlItem. More specifically, if RemoteControl is True, the underlying system copies the RemoteValue to the ProcesControlItem Value to drive it, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is remotely controlled. If RemoteControl is False, the underlying system is not using RemoteValue to drive the ProcessControlItem, but another value that is exposed as the ProcessControlItem Value, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is locally controlled. A client requests (resp. releases) control of the ProcessControlItem by setting RemoteControl to True (resp. False) preferably by invoking the SetRemoteControl Method. If the client does not support methods, then the client sets RemoteControl to True. The underlying system will reset RemoteControl to False if remote control is not activated.

The RemoteControlEnable variable exposes when the underlying system is ready to activate the RemoteControl upon a request by a client. When RemoteControlEnable is False, the underlying system is not ready and will not activate a request to remotely control the ProcessControlItem.
The value set by the client to override the object value.

The Property MaterialRejectionPoints identifies the rejection points of the machine module and their capability in terms of what materials are rejected The Property MaterialRejectionPoints is defined as a list of objects of type MaterialPointType.

The OperatorControl variable qualifies the source of the ProcessControlItem Value when RemoteControl is False, otherwise OperatorControl is undefined. When OperatorControl is True, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is modified by the operator with respect to the nominal value, e.g. NominalRate, a.k.a. design speed for a speed control loop. When OperatorControl is False, the underlying system exposes the information that the ProcessControlItem Value is not modified by the operator.

The RemoteControl variable lets the underlying system expose which system is currently in control of the ProcessControlItem. More specifically, if RemoteControl is True, the underlying system copies the RemoteValue to the ProcesControlItem Value to drive it, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is remotely controlled. If RemoteControl is False, the underlying system is not using RemoteValue to drive the ProcessControlItem, but another value that is exposed as the ProcessControlItem Value, i.e. the ProcessControlItem is locally controlled. A client requests (resp. releases) control of the ProcessControlItem by setting RemoteControl to True (resp. False) preferably by invoking the SetRemoteControl Method. If the client does not support methods, then the client sets RemoteControl to True. The underlying system will reset RemoteControl to False if remote control is not activated.

The RemoteControlEnable variable exposes when the underlying system is ready to activate the RemoteControl upon a request by a client. When RemoteControlEnable is False, the underlying system is not ready and will not activate a request to remotely control the ProcessControlItem.
The value set by the client to override the object value.

When WatchdogEnable is True, if a ProcessControlLoop component’s RemoteControl is True and the time between two consecutive writes of the RemoteAnalogMeasurement is longer than WatchdogTimeout, then the underlying system will generate an alarm, set RemoteControl to False and take control of the loop. When WatchdogEnable is False, no watchdog alarm is generated.
The longest time between two write actions before a watchdog alarm is generated by the underlying system. The value is expressed in milliseconds.

The time in hours a ProductionOrderStateMachine is retained in memory after the production order is complete.

UAMethod.Description: The ReleaseProductionOrder Method is used to make a production order available to a machine module for orchestrated execution in a production line (Process Cell according to ANSI/ISA-88.00.01-2010 Physical Model).

uax:Description.uax:Text: The Production Order Header for the Production Order to be released.
The user name of the machine module where the PO is released.
The result of the execution of the method.

UAMethod.Description: The StartProductionOrder Method is used to start the execution of a production order at a machine module specifying the loading points that input materials will be fed to and the output points where output will be directed.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The Production Order Header for the Production Order to be started.
The user name of the machine module where the PO is started.
The MaterialLoadingPoints where input materials will be fed for the Production Order to be started.
The MaterialOutputPointss where output materials will be directed to for the Production Order to be started.
The result of the execution of the method.

UAMethod.Description: The UnAssignProductionOrder Method is used to unassign a production order previously assigned to an infeed machine module.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The Production Order Header for the Production Order to be unassigned.
The result of the execution of the method.

UAMethod.Description: The UnreleaseProductionOrder Method is used to reverse the effect of the ReleaseProductionOrder method and make a previously released production order unavailable for assignment and production.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The Production Order Header for the Production Order to be unreleased.
The result of the execution of the method.

UAObjectType.Description: The UIInformationType provides graphical specifications required for creating faceplates to display the information made available by the OPC UA Server.

UAMethod.Description: The Method DeleteUIResource permanently removes a UI resource from the underlying system memory.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The name of the UI resource to be deleted from the underlying system.
The extended feedback returning a detailed message in case of execution failure.

UAMethod.Description: The Method LoadUIResource loads a UI resource in the underlying system for visualization. It will override the existing UI resource by the same name.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The name of the UI resource to be created in the underlying system.
The value that the UI resource will obtain in the underlying system, i.e. the SVG file.
The extended feedback returning a detailed message in case of execution failure.

UAVariable.Description: PositionX is the relative horizontal position of the top-left corner of the object rendering in the target visualization scope.
PositionX is the relative vertical position of the top-left corner of the object rendering in the target visualization scope.
PositionZ is the depth of the object rendering in the target visualization scope.
When Resizable is True, the UI resource Width is rescaled based on the actual display size.

UAObject.Description: The UIResources folder contains any number of vectorial images of the object to be rendered in the status/mode defined by the name of the file, e.g. Running.svg is the representation of the object when the status is running.

UAVariable.Description: Width is the width of the object visualization in the target visualization scope.

UAObjectType.Description: The UserInterfaceType provides a generic User Interface description.

UAObject.Description: The control panel area where read-only objects are shown. Objects connected to a ControlPanelVURO by means of a non-hierarchical reference of type IsDisplayedBy are shown in the control panel.
The control panel area where read-write objects are shown. Objects connected to a ControlPanelVURW by means of a non-hierarchical reference of type IsDisplayedBy are shown in the control panel.
The object collecting variables to be displayed in the KPI section. Objects connected to a KPIVU by means of a non-hierarchical reference of type IsDisplayedBy are shown in the KPI display area.

The collection of references to control loops to be displayed. Non-hierarchical references connected to LoopVuReferences by means of a non-hierarchical reference of type IsDisplayedBy are shown in the control panel.
The overview of the UI interface. Objects connected to an OverVU by means of a non-hierarchical reference of type IsDisplayedBy are shown in the overview display.
The zooned view of the UI interface. Objects connected to a ZoomedVU by means of a non-hierarchical reference of type IsDisplayedBy are shown in the zoomed in area.
